newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - GUS shares fall on downbeat outlook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - GUS shares fall on downbeat outlook.

text.p: Retailer and mail order group Great Universal Stores Plc on Thursday saw its shares dive as it reported lower first half profits and warned that tough trading in home shopping meant little chance of a quick turnaround.

Pretax profits fell to 235.6 million pounds ($389.2 million) from 237.5 million in the six months to September 30 1996. Sales rose to 1.21 billion pounds from 1.20 billion. The dividend was increased to 5.5 pence, from 5.0 pence.

GUS, the British market leader in mail order, had already flagged the profit fall in October, but the downbeat trading statement hit the group's shares, which had run up strongly ahead of the results. They stood 17.5 pence lower at 658.5 pence, after falling as much as 20 pence at one stage.
Traders said the damage done by a strong pound to GUS's overseas retailing interests also hit the stock.
"The statement didn't make very pretty reading," said one.

Chairman Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale said trade was still difficult in the home shopping division and the strong pound could affect results from overseas subsidiaries, particularly South Africa and Holland.
"Trading performance for the second half is expected to follow the pattern of the first six months," Wolfson said.
Last month the retailer, best known for its classic Burberry range of clothing, broke with its conservative past by buying U.S. information services firm Experian for $1.7 billion.
The change of pace followed the arrival of Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale as chairman in August, taking over from his older cousin Lord Wolfson of Marylebone.

There has been speculation of more changes to come, but the most pressing question is what plans the group now has for mail order, which is weighted heavily towards the declining agency side of the business.
The sector is seen ripe for restructuring and rival retailer Sears Plc has just put its Freemans mail order business up for sale.

GUS said its British home shopping saw sales fall 2.4 percent on the previous year in a very competitive market. Profit increases by other divisions did not fully compensate for mail order's profit decline, it said.
Home Shopping made operating profits of 61.3 million pounds in the half year, down from 72.4 million. Sales fell to 859.9 million pounds from 870.3 million.
GUS said it was improving warehousing and distribution systems for home shopping and the costs of these changes, which were charged to revenue, depressed trading profits.
Burberrys and Scotch House classic knitwear stores increased profits to 24.4 million pounds from 23.2 million on sales of 130.9 million up from 124.0 million.
Burberrys' results were affected by a decline in Japanese and South East Asian tourist trade in many of its international markets.
Royalty income was affected by the strength of sterling particularly against the yen and the group expected this to have an impact for the rest of the year.

The firm's CCN information services division boosted profits in Britain and overseas. GUS said its purchase in November of Experian, a leading U.S. supplier of credit, marketing and real estate information services, would immediately enhance earnings and generate strong cash flow.
